task: Abstract finite-state continuous-time Markov discrimination under jump, observation, state, and elapsed-time accounting

claims.exact_statement: For two simple hypotheses with iid Bernoulli(p_h) event marks over N fixed slots, the full N-mark path has KL N*D(Ber(p0)||Ber(p1)). Any terminal readout Y that is a function or randomized post-processing of that path has no larger KL and no lower optimal decision risk. In the all-pass design, P_h(Y=1)=p_h^N and, for N>=2 and p0!=p1, D(Ber(p0^N)||Ber(p1^N)) is strictly smaller than the KL of the physical state path and of the full mark record.
assumptions: H in {0,1} is simple and p_h is known with 0<p_h<1 and p0!=p1
The N event marks are conditionally iid Bernoulli(p_h)
Event holding times are independent Exp(lambda) with the same lambda>0 under both hypotheses
The endpoint is a deterministic function of the path; the all-pass CTMC retains only the stage and sticky pass/fail flag
claims.status: conditional theorem proved in proof.md; derives from established KL chain rule, data processing, and Blackwell comparison; no new general information theorem claimed
claims.novelty_boundary: The model-specific stage formulas are reconstructed; data processing and Blackwell dominance are prior art.

costs.full_mark_baseline: N event observations; N jumps; mean time N/lambda; KL N*D(Ber(p0)||Ber(p1))

claims.falsifier: A counterexample satisfying the stated iid mark and common-rate assumptions in which a terminal post-processing has greater KL or lower optimal risk than the full mark path would falsify the claim.
claims.next_gate: Extend the exact resource tradeoff beyond iid Bernoulli marks while retaining explicit state and observation costs; distinguish that from the general full-path data-processing bound.

claims.exact_statement: For N iid Bernoulli event marks under known simple hypotheses p0<p1, a likelihood-ratio threshold on the pass count K, with boundary randomization if needed, maximizes power among binary tests at any prescribed false-positive level. A layered time-homogeneous CTMC storing stage i and count k realizes the decision using N jumps and one terminal readout.
assumptions: H in {0,1} is simple; p0 and p1 are known and 0<p0<p1<1
N event marks are independent conditional on H
Event times are hypothesis-independent Exp(lambda), lambda>0
The test is a binary terminal decision with fixed false-positive constraint
claims.status: conditional theorem proved in proof.md; Neyman-Pearson optimality is established prior art; CTMC implementation and cost count are model reconstruction
claims.novelty_boundary: The threshold rule is the classical Neyman-Pearson lemma; the contribution here is only its explicit finite CTMC realization and cost comparison.

costs.reachable_ctmc_states: N(N+1)/2+2 for the stated layered implementation
costs.state_cost_interpretation: quadratic count of reachable autonomous CTMC states; logarithmic bits to label an individual state; no energy estimate

claims.falsifier: A test using only these N marks with strictly greater power at the same false-positive level than the likelihood-ratio threshold would falsify the claim.
claims.next_gate: Derive minimum state cardinality for each operating point and compare it with observation-limited finite-state transducers; current state count is for one explicit implementation, not a lower bound.

claims.exact_statement: In the all-pass endpoint model, the observable success probability is p^N. If N and p are both unknown, endpoint sampling identifies only their product relation p^N and does not structurally identify N and p separately; for example, (N,p)=(2,1/2) and (N,p)=(4,1/sqrt(2)) both yield 1/4.
assumptions: Only terminal all-pass success/failure is observed
N is an unknown positive integer and p is an unknown number in (0,1)
claims.status: explicit nonidentifiability witness proved in proof.md; model-specific consequence, not a new general identifiability theorem
claims.novelty_boundary: The noninjective parameter map is elementary; no general identifiability result is claimed.

costs.states: 2N+1 for the all-pass CTMC, but N is itself unobserved
costs.observations: one terminal bit; arbitrarily many repeats still identify only p^N if N is unknown

claims.falsifier: A proof that the terminal success probability map (N,p)->p^N is injective over the stated domain would falsify the claim.
claims.next_gate: Characterize which additional observation (known N, intermediate stage output, or time-resolved path) restores structural identifiability under explicit nuisance-parameter assumptions.

claims.exact_statement: There exist distinct three-state cyclic Markov generators Q0 and Q1 with positive off-diagonal rates such that exp(Q0)=exp(Q1) at time T=1. One explicit pair is the circulant generator Q(a,b) with Q0=Q(5,5) and Q1=Q(5+2*pi/sqrt(3),5-2*pi/sqrt(3)).
assumptions: Only the full one-time transition matrix at T=1 is observed
The generator class permits directed three-state cycles
claims.status: explicit algebraic counterexample derived in proof.md; fixed-lag generator nonuniqueness is established Markov embedding prior art
claims.novelty_boundary: The embedding problem and rate nonidentifiability are known; the concrete Fourier-eigenvalue witness is included to make the failure explicit.

costs.observation_cost: full state-to-state transition matrix at one lag, even with arbitrarily many samples, cannot distinguish this pair
costs.additional_discriminator: time-resolved jump directions/exposures or multiple informative lags; costs not optimized here

claims.falsifier: Direct matrix exponentiation showing exp(Q0) differs from exp(Q1) would falsify this witness; the analytic eigenvalue calculation gives identical exponentials.
claims.next_gate: State precise sufficient conditions for generator identifiability in restricted acyclic or reversible CTMC classes; the report does not settle those subclasses.
